title: DataSync and Snow Family
description: Transfer large datasets with AWS DataSync and the Snow Family of edge devices.

data.text: Moving large amounts of data to AWS can be slow over the internet. **AWS DataSync** automates data transfers, and the **Snow Family** provides physical devices for moving terabytes or petabytes of data.

DataSync is an online data transfer service. You deploy an agent on your source storage system, and DataSync handles copying files to Amazon S3, EFS, or FSx. It includes encryption, scheduling, and bandwidth throttling.

data.title: DataSync Features
items: Agent-based transfer from NFS, SMB, or self-managed file systems
Built-in encryption and data integrity checks
Incremental transfers after the initial sync

data.text: The Snow Family is a set of physical devices that you can order from AWS when your data is too large to transfer over the internet efficiently.

cards.title: Snowcone
cards.description: Small, rugged edge device for edge computing and data collection.

cards.title: Snowball
cards.description: Suitcase-sized device for large-scale data transfer.

cards.title: Snowmobile
cards.description: A shipping container on a truck for exabyte-scale migrations.

data.title: Guidelines
items: **DataSync** — for ongoing online transfers, incremental sync, and regular data movement
**Snowcone** — for small edge workloads or harsh environments
**Snowball** — for one-time bulk transfers up to petabytes

data.title: Pro Tip
data.text: Use Snowball Edge Compute Optimized if you want to process data at the edge (e.g., machine learning inference) while transferring it to AWS.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: DataSync automates online file transfers with encryption and scheduling
Snow Family provides physical devices for large-scale data movement
Choose DataSync for ongoing transfers and Snow for one-time bulk migrations
